swap_risks: CRITICAL SUPPLY VOLTAGE RATING: LM358DR is limited to 30 V max (32 V abs max, p.4) whereas TL072IDR supports up to 40 V (42 V abs max, p.10). Installing a 5.5 V CMOS op-amp on a 12 V–24 V rail causes instant breakdown.

CAUTION BANDWIDTH & PHASE MARGIN: GBWP differs by 7.5x (LM358DR: 0.7 MHz p.10 vs TL072IDR: 5.25 MHz p.15); higher-bandwidth replacements can oscillate with capacitive loads or stray feedback capacitance without an isolation resistor.
CAUTION SLEW RATE DIFFERENCE: Slew rate differs by 66.7x (LM358DR: 0.3 V/µs p.10 vs TL072IDR: 20 V/µs p.16); check full-power bandwidth SR / (2π·Vpeak).
engineering_verdict: LM358DR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) and TL072IDR (Texas Instruments, SOIC-8) are Level 2 Functional / Tuning Required replacements: while the footprint is physically compatible, engineering review and passive/circuit adjustments are mandatory due to supply voltage Vs,max drops >20%; GBWP differs >= 3x; slew rate differs >= 3x. Key datasheet deltas: device type is opamp (push-pull) vs opamp (push-pull), supply limit is 30 V (p.5) vs 40 V (p.11), max Vos is 7 mV (p.10) vs 6 mV (p.15), input bias current is 20000 pA (p.10) vs 65 pA (p.15), and Iq/ch is 350 µA (p.10) vs 1400 µA (p.16). Always validate pinout orientation (TOP_VIEW p.3 vs TOP_VIEW p.5), thermal margin (θJA 124.7 vs 147.8 °C/W), and official manufacturer datasheets on hardware prototypes before production release.
